paragraphs: UVeye builds automated inspection systems that scan the full exterior, undercarriage, and tires of a vehicle in seconds. Dealerships use the scans to document pre-existing damage and avoid unnecessary claims. Seaports and logistics hubs use touchless inspections to speed vehicle handoffs and settle disputes. Bus and truck operators run standardized inspections to improve compliance.

A scan combines high-resolution imaging, sensors, and patented AI to surface problems the eye cannot catch. Findings run from tire wear and misalignment to leaks, rust, and underbody damage. Output arrives as images and measurements of dents, scratches, and undercarriage issues. Automatic notifications flag critical issues that need immediate attention.

Brothers Amir and Ohad Hever founded UVeye in 2016. The first application was undercarriage security screening, which grew into a platform that scans whole vehicles. Systems are now deployed across hundreds of dealerships, fleets, rental agencies, and manufacturing lines worldwide. The company names Amazon, General Motors, Volvo, and CarMax among the companies using it. It reports over $380 million raised.
